extracted.intended_audience: public water system owners/operators and State drinking water regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedures for water systems to inventory, plan, prioritize, notify, replace, and report on lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines under the EPA rule. Includes timelines, replacement-rate calculations, public access, and State interactions (shortened/deferred deadlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service line replacement plan — overall requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Water system must create a service line replacement plan by the compliance date in § 141.80(a)(3) and submit a service line replacement plan to the State in accordance with § 141.90(e). The service line replacement plan must be sufficiently detailed to ensure a system is able to comply with the service line inventory and replacement requirements in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan creation and timely State submission are mandatory; plan must enable compliance with inventory and replacement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: strategy for determining material of lead-status-unknown lines
rubrics_metrics.description: The service line replacement plan must include a description of a strategy for determining the material composition of lead status unknown service lines in the service line inventory under paragraph (a) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide methods/approach to resolve unknowns so lines can be categorized for replacement planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: standard operating procedure for full service line replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: The service line replacement plan must include a standard operating procedure for conducting full service line replacement (e.g., techniques to replace service lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include technical procedures, construction/installation methods, sequencing, and other SOP details needed to carry out full replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: communication strategy before replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: The service line replacement plan must include a communication strategy to inform consumers (i.e., persons served at the service connection) and customers before a full or partial lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line replacement consistent with the requirements for notification and mitigation in paragraph (h) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail how and when customers/consumers (including occupants) will be notified prior to replacement work, aligned with paragraph (h) protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: flushing procedure for particulate lead after disturbance/replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: The service line replacement plan must include a procedure for consumers and customers to flush service lines and premise plumbing of particulate lead following disturbance of a lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service line in accordance with § 141.85(f) and following full or partial replacement of a lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line consistent with the requirements for notification and mitigation in paragraph (h) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, consumer-facing flushing protocols tied to the referenced mitigation provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: prioritization strategy for replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: The service line replacement plan must include a strategy to prioritize service line replacement based on factors including, but not limited to, known lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines and community-specific factors, such as populations disproportionately impacted by lead and populations most sensitive to the effects of lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document prioritization criteria (e.g., vulnerable populations, exposure risk, geographic concentration) and how they will be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: funding strategy and customer assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The service line replacement plan must include a funding strategy for conducting service line replacement. Where the water system intends to charge customers for the cost to replace all or a portion of the service line because it is authorized or required to do so under State or local law or water tariff agreement, the funding strategy must include a description of whether and how the water system intends to assist customers who are unable to pay to replace the portion of the service line they own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify funding sources, cost allocation, and any assistance programs or affordability measures for customers unable to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: communication strategy to inform residential and non-residential customers about program
rubrics_metrics.description: The service line replacement plan must include a communication strategy to inform residential and non-residential customers and consumers (e.g., property owners, renters, and tenants) served by the water system about the service line replacement plan and program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address outreach modalities and messaging tailored to different customer types (owners, renters, commercial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: identification of laws/regulations/water tariff agreements affecting access
rubrics_metrics.description: The service line replacement plan must include identification of any laws, regulations, and/or water tariff agreements that affect the water system's ability to gain access to conduct full lead and galvanized requiring replacement service line replacement, including the citation to the specific laws, regulations, or water tariff agreement provisions. This includes identification of any laws, regulations, and/or water tariff agreements that require customer consent and/or require or authorize customer cost-sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific statutory/regulatory/tariff provisions that limit or condition access or customer cost responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: strategy for lead-lined galvanized service lines
rubrics_metrics.description: For any water system that identifies any lead-lined galvanized service lines in the service line inventory as described in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, a strategy to determine the extent of the use of lead-lined galvanized service lines in the distribution system and categorize any lead-lined galvanized service lines as lead pursuant to table 2 to paragraph (d)(6)(iii)(A) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe assessment methods and categorization approach per the rule's table guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan: documentation and specifications for use of a deferred deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: For any water system that is eligible for and plans to use a deferred deadline pursuant to paragraph (d)(5)(vi) of this section, the plan must include documentation to support the system's determination that it is eligible for a deferred deadline, identification of the deferred deadline and associated cumulative average replacement rate, and information supporting the system's determination that replacing lines by an earlier date and faster rate is not feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include numeric calculations (e.g., 10% threshold and 39 per 1,000 metric), deadlines, annual replacement counts, timeframes, and justification showing infeasibility of earlier/faster schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility of the plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The service line replacement plan must be made accessible to the public. Water systems serving greater than 50,000 persons must make the plan available to the public online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the plan available publicly and ensure online availability for large systems (>50,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual updates and State submission of plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems must annually update the service line replacement plan to include any new or updated information and submit the updates to the State on an annual basis in accordance with § 141.90(e). The water system must make the updated plan publicly accessible no later than the deadline to submit the updated plan to the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no changes, systems may certify no updates to the State (with exceptions for deferred deadline holders). Deferred-deadline systems must update specified information every three years. If inventory no longer contains lead/galvanized/unknown lines, systems need not resubmit or certify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory full service line replacement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All water systems must replace all lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines under the control of the water system unless the replacement would leave in place a partial lead service line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems are obligated to fully replace service lines under their control; partial leaves are generally not allowed unless exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement when system has access vs. lack of access documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a water system has access (e.g., legal access, physical access) to conduct full service line replacement, the service line is under its control, and the water system must replace the service line. Where a water system does not have access to conduct full service line replacement, the water system is not required by this subpart to replace the line, but the water system must document the reasons that the water system does not have access and include any specific laws, regulations, and/or water tariff agreements that affect the water system's ability to gain access to conduct full replacement of lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines. The water system must provide this documentation to the State pursuant to § 141.90(e)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document access barriers and cite legal instruments; submit documentation to the State per reporting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable effort to obtain property owner consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a water system has legal access to conduct full service line replacement only if property owner consent is obtained, the water system must make a 'reasonable effort' to obtain property owner consent. A 'reasonable effort' must include at least four attempts to engage the property owner using at least two different methods of communication (e.g., in-person conversation, phone call, text message, email, written letter, postcard, or information left at the door such as a door hanger) before the applicable deadline of mandatory service line replacement as described in paragraph (d)(4) of this section. The State may require systems to conduct additional attempts and may require specific outreach methods to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document outreach attempts and methods; be prepared to provide this documentation to the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer replacement after change in ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Within six months of any change in ownership of the property, the water system must offer full service line replacement to any new property owner. Within one year of any change in ownership of the property, the system must make a 'reasonable effort' to obtain the property owner's consent as described in paragraph (d)(3)(i). If the water system is unable to obtain consent from the current property owner after making a 'reasonable effort' to obtain it, the water system is not required under this subpart to replace the line. This paragraph continues to apply until all lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines are replaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use service initiation/transfer to identify ownership changes; document offers and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to replace lines under system control (10 program years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline for water systems to replace all lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines under the control of the water system is no later than 10 program years after the compliance date specified in § 141.80(a)(3) unless the system is subject to a different deadline under paragraphs (d)(5)(v) and (vi) of this section. Water systems must start mandatory service line replacement programs no later than the compliance date specified in § 141.80(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and commence replacement programs promptly to meet the 10-program-year target unless State sets shortened or deferred deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid replacement when lead discovered in otherwise non-lead inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line is discovered when the system's inventory is comprised of only non-lead service lines, the system must update the replacement pool and conduct a full service line replacement of the affected service line as soon as practicable but no later than 180 days after the date the service line is discovered. Where not practicable (e.g., freezing ground), the system may request State approval for an extension of no later than one year after discovery; the request must be made no later than 90 days after discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely update inventories and complete replacements; follow extension-request timing rules if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum cumulative average annual replacement rate (10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system must replace lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines at an average annual replacement rate of at least 10 percent calculated across a cumulative period unless the system is subject to a shortened replacement rate or eligible for a deferred replacement rate in accordance with paragraphs (d)(5)(v) and (vi) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and demonstrate at least a 10% cumulative average annual replacement rate unless otherwise directed by State decisions or deferred/shortened provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of cumulative percent and cumulative average replacement rate
rubrics_metrics.description: To calculate the cumulative percent of service lines replaced, at the end of each mandatory service line replacement 'program year' water systems must divide the total number of lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines replaced thus far in the program by the number of service lines within the replacement pool. Program years defined (first is from compliance date to end of next calendar year; thereafter calendar year). The cumulative average replacement rate is assessed first at the end of the third program year and is calculated by dividing the cumulative percent of service lines replaced by the number of completed program years (or three for the first assessment). Annually thereafter divide the most recent cumulative percent by number of completed program years. Except as provided, the cumulative average replacement rate must be 10 percent or greater each program year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified timing and math for cumulative assessment; initial assessment at end of third program year. Keep documentation to support calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception when system has replaced all under-control lines and lacks access to remainder
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system is not required to meet the cumulative average replacement rate where, after the compliance date, the system has replaced all lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines in the replacement pool that are under the control of the system, identified all unknown service lines in the inventory, and documented and submitted to the State the reasons the system currently does not have access to conduct full replacement of the remaining service lines. When lines come under control, the system is required to replace them as described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure complete documentation and State submission to qualify for this exception; replacement obligations resume when lines come under system control.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-determined shortened deadline and replacement rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the State determines that a shortened replacement deadline is feasible for a water system, the system must replace service lines by the State-determined deadline and by a faster minimum replacement rate. The State must make this determination in writing and may set a shortened deadline at any time. The system's average annual replacement rate is calculated by dividing 100 by the number of years needed to meet the shortened deadline, expressed as a percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with written State determinations; use the 100/years calculation to set the required average annual rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred deadlines eligibility and calculation (39 per 1,000 cap)
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system may defer service line replacement past the 10-program-year deadline if replacing 10 percent of the total number of known lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines results in an annual number of replacements that exceeds 39 per 1,000 service connections. The number of annual replacements corresponding to 39 per 1,000 can be calculated by multiplying the number of service connections by 0.039. Years needed to complete replacement = total known lines in replacement pool divided by calculated annual replacements. The minimum cumulative average replacement rate equals 100 divided by the number of years needed to achieve replacing at the 39-per-1,000 rate, expressed as a percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified numeric method to determine deferred-deadline feasibility and compute the deferred replacement rate; include these calculations in the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred deadline documentation and State review
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems eligible for and planning to use a deferred deadline must include supporting information in the initial plan and subsequent updates, identify an annual replacement rate no less than 39 per 1,000 service connections, and as soon as practicable but no later than the end of the second program year and every three years thereafter, the State must determine in writing whether the deferred deadline and rate are the fastest feasible and either approve continued use or set a shorter deadline and rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required documentation in plan; expect periodic State review and possible requirement to adopt faster rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of replacement pool composition and update rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To calculate the replacement pool, systems must add the total number of lead, galvanized requiring replacement, and lead status unknown service lines in the baseline inventory submitted by the compliance date. The water system must not subtract lead or galvanized requiring replacement service lines from the replacement pool when they are replaced, and must not subtract service lines that are not under the control of the system. At the beginning of each program year, update the replacement pool according to recategorizations: unknown identified as non-lead subtract; unknown identified as lead or galvanized recategorize but do not change count; non-lead discovered to be lead add; lead discovered to be non-lead subtract; each entire service line counts only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow annual recategorization rules consistently; be cautious that replacements do not reduce the replacement pool count unless specifically recategorized to non-lead per rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of annual number of replacements required
rubrics_metrics.description: To calculate the number of lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines a system is required to replace in a given program year, divide the number of service lines in the most up-to-date replacement pool (calculated at the beginning of each program year) by the total number of years remaining under paragraph (d)(4) to complete mandatory service line replacement (e.g., 10 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the replacement-pool count at start of program year and remaining years to compute annual required replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting only full service line replacements for cumulative totals
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating the cumulative average replacement rate, the water system may only include full service line replacements of lead or galvanized requiring replacement service lines when counting the number of service lines replaced. A replacement counts as a full service line replacement only if, after the replacement, the entire service line can be categorized in the inventory as non-lead under paragraph (a)(3)(iii) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial replacements, connector-only replacements, reclassifications, or lining/coating are not full replacements and must not be counted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization rules for mixed-ownership service lines (Table 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must count each entire service line once; Table 2 defines how to categorize the entire service line depending on system-owned portion and customer-owned portion materials (e.g., system-owned lead + customer-owned galvanized requiring replacement = Lead; system-owned non-lead + customer-owned lead = Lead, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the table rules when portions have different materials to determine the line's overall categorization for counting/replacement purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for counting a full replacement when disconnected but not removed
rubrics_metrics.description: A full service line replacement is counted where a non-lead service line is installed for use and the lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line is disconnected from the water main or other service line. If the lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line is disconnected from the water main or system-owned portion of the service line but not removed, the water system must be subject to a State or local law or have a written policy to preclude the water system from reconnecting the lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line to the water main or other service line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure legal/policy safeguards against reconnection if the removed portion remains physically present but disconnected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting full replacement at abandoned properties
rubrics_metrics.description: A full service line replacement may be counted where a system physically disconnects a service line that is not in use and the water system does not install a new non-lead service line because there is no service line in use (e.g., at an abandoned property). If the disconnected lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line is not removed, the water system must be subject to a State or local law or have a written policy to preclude the water system from reconnecting the disconnected service line (i.e., a new non-lead service line must be installed if active use is to resume).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document disconnection and legal/policy measures to prevent reconnection; track such counts in inventory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions that must NOT be counted as full service line replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems must not count the following as a full service line replacement: (1) Where the service line is partially replaced as defined in § 141.2; (2) Where a lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or unknown service line is determined to be a non-lead service line; (3) Where only a lead connector is replaced; (4) Where pipe lining or coating technologies are used while the lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line remains in use; (5) Where a water system does not replace a lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line because it is not be under the control of the system as described in paragraph (d)(2) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include partial work, connector-only upgrades, or temporary lining/coating as full replacements in replacement-rate calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of lead connectors encountered during work
rubrics_metrics.description: The water system must replace any lead connector when encountered during planned or unplanned water system infrastructure work unless the connector is not under the control of the system (e.g., where the system does not have and cannot obtain access to conduct the connector replacement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon replacement, follow risk mitigation (§ 141.85(f)(2)) and update connector material/location in the inventory; comply with any State/local laws requiring additional connector replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer-initiated partial replacements — system obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If State or local laws or water tariff agreements do not prevent customer-initiated partial replacements, then: (a) If notified a customer intends to conduct a partial replacement, the water system must replace the remaining portion at the same time or as soon as practicable but no later than 45 days from the date the customer conducted the partial replacement; provide notification and risk mitigation per paragraph (h); notify the State within 30 days if it cannot meet the 45-day deadline and complete the replacement no later than 180 days. (b) If notified of a customer-initiated replacement within previous six months and system-owned portion remains, the system must replace remaining portion within 45 days of awareness, provide mitigation within 24 hours, and notify State within 30 days if cannot meet the deadline (complete replacement no later than 180 days). (c) If the system learns of a customer-initiated replacement that occurred more than six months in the past, this paragraph does not require the system to complete replacement now, but the remaining portion must be identified in the inventory and replaced per paragraph (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track customer-initiated work and meet strict timelines for system completion and notification; provide urgent mitigation where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on water-system-conducted partial replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: This paragraph prohibits water systems from conducting a partial lead service line replacement or a partial galvanized requiring replacement service line replacement as defined under § 141.2 unless it is conducted as part of an emergency repair or in coordination with planned infrastructure work that impacts service lines, excluding planned infrastructure work solely for the purposes of lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line replacement. Where a water system has access to conduct full service line replacement as specified in paragraph (d)(2) of this section, the water system must fully replace the service line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial replacements by the system are allowed only in emergencies or as part of broader planned work (not when planned solely to avoid full replacement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dielectric coupling requirement for partial replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a water system conducts a partial replacement of a lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line, the system must include a dielectric coupling separating the remaining service line and the replaced service line (i.e., newly installed service line) to prevent galvanic corrosion unless the replaced service line is made of plastic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate dielectric couplings when conducting partial replacements to avoid electrochemical corrosion unless plastic replacement obviates need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and mitigation — planned partial replacement timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a water system plans to partially replace a lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line in coordination with planned infrastructure work that impacts service lines, the water system must provide written notice to the property owner, or the owner's authorized agent, as well as non-owner occupant(s) served by the affected service line at least 45 days prior to the replacement. Before the affected service line is returned to service, the water system must provide written notification that explains that consumers may experience a temporary increase of lead levels and that meets the content requirements of § 141.85(a)(1)(ii) through (iv) and contact information for the water system. The system must provide written information about a flushing procedure, provide a pitcher filter or point-of-use device certified to reduce lead with six months of replacement cartridges and instructions for use (to every residential and non-residential unit if multi-unit), and offer to collect a follow-up tap sample between three and six months after the partial replacement (first- and fifth-liter paired sample after at least six hours stagnation per § 141.86(b)); provide results per § 141.85(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver notices and mitigation materials on specified timelines; if multi-unit, posting may be used; provide certified filters and sample offer per protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and mitigation — emergency partial replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any water system that creates a partial replacement due to an emergency repair must provide notice and risk mitigation measures to the persons served by the affected service line in accordance with paragraphs (h)(1)(i) through (iv) of this section before the affected service line is returned to service. The water system must offer to the property owner to replace the partial service line created by the emergency repair within 45 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same mitigation items as for planned partials (filters, flushing, sampling offers) and offer timely full replacement to owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and mitigation — full service line replacement timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any water system that conducts a full lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line replacement must provide written notice to the persons served by the affected service line before the affected service line is returned to service; written notice must be provided to the owner or the owner's authorized agent, no later than 30 days following completion of the replacement. The notification must explain potential temporary increases in lead, meet content requirements of § 141.85(a)(1)(ii) through (iv), provide flushing procedure information, provide a certified pitcher filter or point-of-use device with six months of replacement cartridges and instructions to every residential and non-residential unit in multi-unit buildings, and offer to collect a follow-up tap sample between three and six months after completion (first-liter sample after at least six hours stagnation per § 141.86(b)); provide results per § 141.85(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pre-return and owner follow-up notices, mitigation tools, and sampling offers as specified; ensure distribution to all units in multi-unit buildings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting to State to demonstrate compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: To demonstrate compliance with paragraphs (a) through (h) of this section, a water system must report to the State the information specified in § 141.90(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the reporting provisions in § 141.90(e) to submit required documentation and data to the State.
